mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares longitudinal and transverse waves?

options.A: In longitudinal waves, particle displacement is parallel to wave propagation; in transverse waves, displacement is perpendicular.
options.B: In longitudinal waves, particle displacement is perpendicular to wave propagation; in transverse waves, displacement is parallel.
options.C: Both longitudinal and transverse waves have particle displacement parallel to propagation.
options.D: Both longitudinal and transverse waves have particle displacement perpendicular to propagation.

mcqs.answer: In longitudinal waves, particle displacement is parallel to wave propagation; in transverse waves, displacement is perpendicular.
mcqs.explanation: In a longitudinal wave the particles oscillate back‑and‑forth along the same direction the wave travels, whereas in a transverse wave the particles move up and down (or side to side) perpendicular to the direction of travel. Options B, C and D describe the opposite or incorrect relationships.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify wavelength, frequency, amplitude and period
mcqs.question: A wave is described by the equation y = 0.05 sin[2π(4t – 0.2x)] where y is in metres, t in seconds and x in metres. Which set gives the correct wavelength, frequency, amplitude and period of this wave?
mcqs.explanation: The equation y = A sin(2πft – 2πx/λ) gives A = 0.05 m. Comparing, 2πf = 2π·4 ⇒ f = 4 Hz, and 2π/λ = 2π·0.2 ⇒ λ = 1/0.2 = 5 m. Period T = 1/f = 0.25 s. Only option A matches all four quantities. The other options contain incorrect values for one or more parameters.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines wave motion?

options.A: Transfer of matter from one place to another without any energy transfer.
options.B: Periodic disturbance that propagates through a medium or vacuum with transfer of energy but no net transport of matter.
options.C: Random motion of particles in a fluid.
options.D: Continuous motion of a single particle along a straight line.

mcqs.answer: Periodic disturbance that propagates through a medium or vacuum with transfer of energy but no net transport of matter.
mcqs.explanation: Wave motion is a periodic disturbance that travels through a medium (or vacuum for electromagnetic waves) carrying energy, while the individual particles of the medium oscillate about their equilibrium positions and do not undergo net displacement. Option B captures this definition; the others describe unrelated phenomena.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes mechanical waves from electromagnetic waves?

options.A: Mechanical waves can travel in vacuum, whereas electromagnetic waves require a material medium.
options.B: Mechanical waves require a material medium for propagation, while electromagnetic waves can propagate in vacuum.
options.C: Both types require a material medium, but only mechanical waves involve electric fields.
options.D: Electromagnetic waves are longitudinal, while mechanical waves are always transverse.

mcqs.answer: Mechanical waves require a material medium for propagation, while electromagnetic waves can propagate in vacuum.
mcqs.explanation: Mechanical waves (e.g., sound, seismic) need a material medium because they rely on particle interactions. Electromagnetic waves (light, radio) are oscillations of electric and magnetic fields and can travel through empty space. Options A, C and D are incorrect statements.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes a transverse wave and distinguishes it from a longitudinal wave?

options.A: In a transverse wave, particle displacement is parallel to the direction of wave travel; in a longitudinal wave, it is perpendicular.
options.B: In a transverse wave, particle displacement is perpendicular to the direction of wave travel; in a longitudinal wave, it is parallel.
options.C: Both transverse and longitudinal waves have particle displacement parallel to wave travel.
options.D: Both transverse and longitudinal waves have particle displacement perpendicular to wave travel.

mcqs.answer: In a transverse wave, particle displacement is perpendicular to the direction of wave travel; in a longitudinal wave, it is parallel.
mcqs.explanation: Transverse waves involve particle motion at right angles to the direction the wave moves (e.g., waves on a string). Longitudinal waves involve particle motion along the same line as wave propagation (e.g., sound). Option B states this correctly; the other options invert or ignore the distinction.

mcqs.question: A sound wave traveling through air is an example of which type of wave, and what is the direction of particle vibration relative to the direction of wave propagation?

options.A: Transverse wave; particles vibrate perpendicular to propagation.
options.B: Longitudinal wave; particles vibrate parallel to propagation.
options.C: Transverse wave; particles vibrate parallel to propagation.
options.D: Longitudinal wave; particles vibrate perpendicular to propagation.

mcqs.answer: Longitudinal wave; particles vibrate parallel to propagation.
mcqs.explanation: Sound in air is a longitudinal wave: the air molecules oscillate back and forth along the same line that the wave travels, i.e., parallel to the direction of propagation. Hence option B is correct; the other options misclassify the wave type or the vibration direction.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify wavelength, frequency, amplitude and period
mcqs.question: A rope fixed at both ends shows three complete loops (antinodes) along its 1.5 m length when vibrated at 30 Hz. If the amplitude of the standing wave is 2 cm, what are the wavelength, frequency, amplitude and period of the wave?
mcqs.explanation: For a rope fixed at both ends, L = n·λ/2 where n = number of loops = 3. Thus λ = 2L/n = 2×1.5/3 = 1.0 m. Frequency is given as 30 Hz, so period T = 1/f = 0.033 s. Amplitude is 2 cm = 0.02 m. Option A matches all values; the others contain at least one incorrect quantity.

mcqs.question: During a stadium "wave", each spectator stands up and sits down in sequence, creating a visible ripple that travels around the arena. Which statement best describes the type of wave motion exhibited by this phenomenon?

options.A: It is a longitudinal wave because the crowd moves in the direction of the wave.
options.B: It is a transverse wave because the individual motion (standing up) is perpendicular to the direction the ripple travels.
options.C: It is not a wave because there is no medium.
options.D: It is an electromagnetic wave because it involves energy transfer without matter.

mcqs.answer: It is a transverse wave because the individual motion (standing up) is perpendicular to the direction the ripple travels.
mcqs.explanation: The stadium "wave" is analogous to a transverse wave: the visible disturbance (people standing) moves around the stadium, while each person's motion (vertical) is perpendicular to the direction of travel. Hence option B is correct. Options A, C and D mischaracterize the nature of the phenomenon.
